Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 82, verses 1–5:

(p-6083) In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Surah al-Infitar (The Cleaving)

It is Meccan, and its verses number nineteen.

(p-6084) In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

On the interpretation of His, the Exalted, saying:

[1–5] ﴿When the sky is cleaved asunder﴾ ﴿and when the stars are scattered﴾ [al-Infitar: 2] ﴿and when the seas are burst forth﴾ [al-Infitar: 3] ﴿and when the graves are overturned﴾ [al-Infitar: 4] ﴿a soul will know what it has put forward and what it has kept back﴾ [al-Infitar: 5]

﴿When the sky is cleaved asunder﴾, i.e., split open, as in the verse ﴿and the day the sky will split open with clouds﴾ [al-Furqan: 25].

﴿And when the stars are scattered﴾ [al-Infitar: 2], i.e., they fall away. The word al-intithar (scattering) is a metaphor for the removal of the stars, as they are likened to pearls whose string has been cut. It is either an explicit (musarrahah) or an implicit (makniyyah) metaphor.

﴿And when the seas are burst forth﴾ [al-Infitar: 3], i.e., some of them are opened into others, the barrier being removed by the quaking and trembling of the earth.

﴿And when the graves are overturned﴾ [al-Infitar: 4], i.e., they are searched and their dead are brought out.

Al-Shihab said: That is, the earth with which they were filled and which was over their dead is removed, so that they open and those buried in them come out. This is the meaning of al-ba'thara (overturning), and its real sense is the scattering of earth or the like, which occurs only to bring out something beneath it. It may be mentioned while both its meaning and what it entails are intended together, as here. It may also be used figuratively for resurrecting and bringing out, as in Surah al-Adiyat. The difference between the two is that here it is attributed to the graves, so it is used in its literal sense; and there it is attributed to what is in them, so it is a metaphor for what has been mentioned.

He then said: Some imams, such as al-Zamakhshari and al-Suhayli, held that it is a compound of two words by abbreviation. Such formations are common in the Arabic language and are called naht (blending). Its origin is (buʻitha) and (uthira), meaning: it was stirred and brought out. It has parallels such as basmala (saying "bismillah"), hawqala (saying "la hawla wa la quwwata illa billah"), and damʻaza (saying "adama Allahu ʻizzahu"). Thus, on this view, its meaning is both digging up and bringing out together. It is not objected to this that the letter ra' is not among the letters of augmentation, as Abu Hayyan supposed, for there is a difference between compounding/blending two words and adding to some of the root letters of a single word, as he elaborated in al-Muzhir, citing the imams of the language.

﴿A soul will know what it has put forward and what it has kept back﴾ [al-Infitar: 5], i.e., for that day, whether of righteous or evil deeds, ﴿and what it has kept back﴾ [al-Infitar: 5], i.e., what it has left undone of good or evil. Or the meaning is: what it has put forward of good deeds in which it did not fall short, and "what it has kept back" means what it fell short in. The knowledge intended by putting forward and holding back is finding the recompense for both, and the realisation of the fulfilment of the promise concerning them.

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 82, verses 6–8:

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, Exalted is He:

[6–8] ﴿O mankind, what has deceived you concerning your Lord, the Generous?﴾ ﴿Who created you, proportioned you, and balanced you?﴾ [al-Infitar: 7] ﴿In whatever form He willed, He assembled you.﴾ [al-Infitar: 8]

﴿O mankind, what has deceived you concerning your Lord, the Generous?﴾ That is: what thing has deceived you and emboldened you to disobey Him and to turn away from your innate nature (fitrah)? "The Generous" is mentioned for emphasis in forbidding delusion, because it means the Mighty, the Majestic, the One perfect in His attributes. Whoever is like this is deserving that His punishment be feared and His vengeance and torment be dreaded, especially since He has great blessings and complete power, which increase the awe, as He said: ﴿Who created you, proportioned you﴾ [al-Infitar: 7], that is, He made you upright, with limbs and strength in balance. The root of taswiyah (proportioning) is making things equal, so that they are in accordance with wisdom and its requirements, by giving them what completes them. ﴿And balanced you﴾ [al-Infitar: 7], that is, He made you moderate, proportionate in creation, of upright stature, unlike the beasts. It is also read with the lighter form (ʿadalaka), which has the same meaning as the intensive form, or it means He turned you from the creation of others to a good creation, by which you were distinguished over the rest of the animals. ﴿In whatever form He willed, He assembled you﴾ [al-Infitar: 8], that is, in whatever form He willed, He assembled you upon it. The meaning is that He assembled you in a form which is the most wondrous and marvellous of forms. So "ayy" (which form) is interrogative, the prepositional phrase is attached to "rakkabaka" (He assembled you), and "ma" is superfluous, and the clause "shaa'a" (He willed) is a qualifier of "sura" (form). The intent is that He who created this wondrous creation, proportioned it and balanced it by His power and decree, until He perfected its form in that composition, is deserving that His might be guarded against, His seizure be feared, and that He be dreaded with the utmost dread.

Note:

Imam Ibn al-Qayyim said in (al-Jawab al-Kafi), in the discussion that the Qur'an, from beginning to end, explicitly establishes the ordering of reward with good and evil, and of the cosmic decrees, upon causes, what completes it: so let one beware of deceiving oneself regarding these causes, and this is among the most important matters, for the servant knows that disobedience and heedlessness are among the causes harmful to him in his worldly life and his Hereafter, without doubt. But his soul deceives him.

Then he mentioned, among the types of the deluded, one who is deceived by a corrupt understanding that he and his like derived from the texts of the Qur'an and the Sunnah, and so they relied upon it. He said: like the deception of some ignorant people by His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿O mankind, what has deceived you concerning your Lord, the Generous?﴾, so that one says: "He honoured him." Some of them may say: "He taught the deluded one his argument." This is foul ignorance. What deceived him concerning his Lord is delusion (al-ghurur), namely Satan, his commanding soul, his ignorance and his desire. Almighty and Glorious is He, who used the word "the Generous," which is the great, obeyed Lord, for whom one should not be deluded and whose right should not be neglected. This deluded person placed "delusion" in other than its proper place, and was deceived by one about whom one should not be deceived. End of quotation.

Concerning this kind of delusion, it is obligatory upon the servant, as al-Ghazali said, to employ fear, so that he frightens himself with the wrath of God and His great punishment, and says: He, although He is the Forgiver of sin and the Accepter of repentance, is severe in punishment. And: He, although He is Generous, has eternally consigned the disbelievers to the Fire forever. Although their disbelief did not harm Him, He has imposed torment, trials, diseases, ailments, poverty and hunger upon a number of His servants in this world, while He is able to remove them. So whoever has such a custom with His servants, and He has warned me of His punishment, how should I not fear Him? And how should I be deceived by Him?

Fear and hope are two leaders and drivers which move people to action. Whatever does not move to action is mere wishful thinking and delusion, and the hope of the whole creation is the cause of their lethargy, the cause of their turning to this world, the cause of their turning away from God Exalted, and their neglect of striving for the Hereafter; this is delusion. It has been related that delusion will overcome the hearts of the last of this Ummah. And so it has been: the people in the first ages used to persevere in worship, and "they give what they give while their hearts are fearful that they will return to their Lord" [al-Mu'minun: 60]. They feared for themselves, and they were, all night and day, in obedience to God, striving greatly in piety and caution against doubtful matters and desires, and weeping over themselves in solitude. But now you see the creation secure, joyful, reassured and unafraid, despite their devotion to sins, their immersion in the world and their turning away from God Exalted, claiming that they are confident in the generosity and grace of God Exalted, hoping for His pardon and forgiveness, as though they claim that they have known of His grace and generosity what the prophets, the Companions and the righteous predecessors did not know. If this matter were attained by wishes and gained by ease, then upon what was the weeping, fear and sorrow of those people?!

Then he said: The Qur'an from beginning to end is a warning and a admonition, and no reflecter reflects upon it without his sorrow lengthening and his fear growing great, even if he believes in what is in it. And you see people reciting it hastily: they bring out the letters from their articulation points and dispute over their lowering, raising and putting in the accusative, as if they were reciting a poem of the Arabs, not concerned with reflecting on its meanings or acting by what is in it. And is there in the world a delusion greater than this? End of quotation.

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, Exalted is He:

[6–8] ﴿O mankind, what has deceived you concerning your Lord, the Generous?﴾ ﴿Who created you, proportioned you, and balanced you?﴾ [al-Infitar: 7] ﴿In whatever form He willed, He assembled you.﴾ [al-Infitar: 8]

It is also read with the lighter form (ʿadalaka), which has the same meaning as the intensive form, or it means He turned you from the creation of others to a good creation, by which you were distinguished over the rest of the animals. ﴿In whatever form He willed, He assembled you﴾ [al-Infitar: 8], that is, in whatever form He willed, He assembled you upon it. The discussion of His saying, the Exalted:

[9–12] ﴿Nay, but you deny the Recompense.﴾ ﴿And indeed, over you are guardians,﴾ ﴿noble recorders,﴾ ﴿who know what you do.﴾

﴿Nay, but you deny the Recompense.﴾ The Imam said: That is, let nothing deceive you or delude you. Rather, the abundance of your Lord's bounty and His wisdom in His generosity should point you to, and suggest to your soul, that you will be resurrected on another day for reward or punishment. What actually occurs from you, O human being, is obstinacy and denial of the Recompense (al-din), that is, the judgment (al-jaza'). That is, turning away deliberately and stubbornly from what the first instinct calls you to, and from the proof that the Messengers establish and the argument that the Prophets bring, even though God the Exalted has not left any of your deeds unguarded, but has recorded and counted it against you until He pays you its recompense, as He said: ﴿And indeed, over you are guardians﴾ [al-Infitar: 10], that is, watchers who guard your deeds and count them against you, ﴿noble recorders﴾ [al-Infitar: 11], that is, they write down what you say.

﴿who know what you do﴾ [al-Infitar: 12], that is, of good or evil, meaning they count it against you, so they neither neglect nor forget.

Al-Razi said: God the Exalted has ordered His affairs with His servants according to how they deal with one another among themselves, because that is more eloquent in establishing the meaning for them. Since the most eloquent way for them in reckoning is the bringing forth of a book with witnesses, they were addressed with the like of this regarding what they will be reckoned for on the Day of Resurrection: books will be laid out for them, and there will be present there angels who testify against them, just as the trustworthy witnesses of the sultan testify against one who disobeys him and opposes his command, and they say to him: "The king gave you such and such, and did such and such for you, and then you opposed him and did such and such." So it is likewise here. And God knows the reality of that best. End of quotation.

It is not hidden that the Noble Guardians and their recording are among the unseen (al-ghayb) which cannot be comprehended, so belief in them is obligatory, as it has been reported, with the entrusting of their true nature to their Creator, the Exalted. And among the superfluities in knowledge is excessive elaboration on what cannot be grasped by reflection, and blackening the faces of the pages with it. And success is from God, glorified is He.
